To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the bit error rate of a flash memory is a strong function of the number and type of program-erase operations it has gone through, and that the write amplification due to the protection schemes can be as high as 50%.
the lifetime of flash memory can be significantly improved by leaving bit errors alone and correcting them only when a threshold of errors is accumulated.
write amplification due to error correction and scrubbing can significantly reduce the lifetime of flash memory.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of ECC and scrubbing on the lifetime of flash memory.
understanding and quantifying the trade-offs between the protection schemes, write endurance, and lifetime of flash memory.
the impact of write amplification due to various ECC and scrubbing schemes on the reliability of flash memory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ECC is not the solution.
write amplification due to the ECC is a significant concern and should be addressed in order to maximize the lifetime of the flash memory device.
the protection schemes are effective only if they are used in conjunction with a scheme that limits the accumulation of bit errors in a page.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lifetime of flash memory can be improved by up to 50% by considering the effects of ECC, write amplification due to scrubbing, as well as the time-varying reliability of flash memory.
the reliability of flash memory is time dependent and the write amplification due to protection schemes is significant.
write amplification should be considered in any protection scheme design.
The main takeaway from our work is that
write amplification due to protection schemes must be considered when evaluating the effectiveness of these protection schemes.
the protection scheme should be carefully chosen based on the application's workload and lifetime requirements.
the reliability of flash memory is not only a function of the total number of program-erases but also of the workload and protection schemes used.
